 SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( SPY ) recorded a net outflow of $11.62 billion in Wednesday's session, with gross ETF activity of $11.62 billion all on the sell side. SPY increased no positions and decreased 502, leaving its $783.49 billion portfolio trimmed across the board rather than repositioned.

 The largest sales were Apple ( AAPL ) at $948.0 million, Microsoft ( MSFT ) at $695.6 million and NVIDIA ( NVDA ) at $673.3 million, followed by Amazon ( AMZN ) at $484.4 million and Broadcom ( AVGO ) at $310.5 million. None of the five was a new position or a full exit; each remained a top holding, with Apple at 8.15% of assets, Microsoft at 5.98% and NVIDIA at 5.79%. 
 How does SPY invest? 
 SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( SPY ) is an Equity US fund in the Equity asset class holding 503 stocks, with 37.1% of assets in its 10 largest holdings. Technology accounts for 36.3% of classified stocks, Financial Services 12.3% and Healthcare 10.4%, and the mix is 99.8% large cap, 0.2% mid cap and 0.0% small cap. Its expense ratio is 0.09%, and top holdings are Apple at 8.15%, Microsoft at 5.98%, NVIDIA at 5.79%, Amazon at 4.16% and Broadcom at 2.67%. The fund has a GF Score of 87, a P/E of 22.92, a P/B of 4.5, a dividend yield of 1.06% and a year-to-date return of 5.8%.
